title: Sandboxed pilot: data handling & contract rider notes
content:
Purpose:
This is a working playbook for a ‘sandboxed pilot’ engagement with regulated customers where we minimize PII persistence and provide a small contract rider (single-page) that can be appended to the standard SOW/DPA.

Background/context:
- Use case: customer wants to evaluate inference quality of a conversational assistant over a 6–8 week pilot. They will upload product docs and invite internal users.
- Ask from customer: guarantee no long-term storage of raw prompts/outputs, ability to delete dataset on request, audit logs for access, and a short DPA addendum that outlines retention windows and data flows.
- Constraints: customer is evaluating hosted API first (fastest), may later request Dedicated or Private deployment. Legal prefers simple, auditable commitments for pilot phase.

High-level recommendation (pilot mode):
- Default mode: Ephemeral prompt capture + short-term audit logs.
- Store generated outputs and prompts in ephemeral sandbox for 14 days by default.
- Retain minimal system logs (request id, model used, tokens billed, latency, route) for 90 days for operational troubleshooting and billing reconciliation. Logs must be aggregated (no raw prompt text) unless explicit flag enabled by customer.
- Optional extended analytics (anonymized transcripts, quality labels) can be exported by customer at any time and persisted on their storage (S3) via connector.

Data categories & handling (practical):
1) Customer-provided documents (training/reference corpus)
   - Storage: encrypted at rest in segregated customer bucket.
   - Retention: until pilot end + 7 days buffer then auto-delete unless customer requests archival.
   - Access: only services with customer-scoped credentials; redaction tooling available to remove specific documents.

2) Prompts / conversational messages
   - Default: not persisted beyond ephemeral cache for inference and logs. Ephemeral cache TTL = 24 hours for active sessions (to support continuity).
   - Pilot retention option: customer can opt-in to 14-day retention for debugging. Opt-in must be explicit in onboarding sheet.

3) Model outputs
   - Default: ephemeral and tied to prompts; not written to durable store. If exported (by UI or API) they are delivered to customer-managed export destination.

4) Observability & telemetry (non-text metrics)
   - Store token-level metrics, per-request latency, error codes for 90 days. No raw text saved unless debug flag set.

5) Debug snapshots / support access
   - Creation: only upon explicit customer request and with an approval workflow (customer signs support snapshot form).
   - Retention: 7 days after snapshot creation, then auto-delete.

Technology controls and implementation notes:
- Encryption: AES-256 at rest; TLS 1.2+ in transit. Keys managed in KMS with per-tenant key wrapping for Dedicated/Private.
- Deletion semantics: soft-delete marker + background purge job. For hosted pilots, purge job runs nightly; complete wipe within 48 hours after purge date.
- Redaction helpers: line-level and pattern (SSN, email, credit-card) detectors baked into upload pipeline. Redaction is best-effort (documented false-positive risk).
- Prefix/KV cache: ensure customer prompt prefixes are isolated per-tenant and not merged into global cache. KV cache eviction policy must support TTL consistent with ephemeral windows.

Suggested pilot retention defaults (summary table style in text):
- Prompts/Outputs (default ephemeral): 14 days (customer opt-in required to extend)
- Debug snapshots: 7 days (on request only)
- Aggregated telemetry / billing logs: 90 days
- Customer reference docs: pilot duration + 7 days

Minimal SRE/SE runbook for onboarding pilot (short checklist):
- [ ] Create tenant project with tenant-tagged storage and KMS key
- [ ] Enable ‘ephemeral pilot’ feature flag in routing layer
- [ ] Set cache TTL to 24h for session continuity and full eviction at 14d
- [ ] Configure logging pipeline to redact text fields by default and route raw-text-to-encrypted-bucket only if support snapshot approved
- [ ] Send onboarding checklist and opt-in form to customer (see linked template)

Contract rider (one-page) — suggested language (draft):
"Pilot Data Handling Rider (draft)
1. Purpose: This rider governs handling of Customer Data during the Pilot.
2. Definitions: ‘Customer Data’ means prompts, uploads, and user-entered content. ‘Pilot Data’ refers to data collected solely for the duration of the Pilot.
3. Retention: Provider will retain Pilot Data for no longer than 14 days by default. Aggregated metrics and billing records (without raw text) may be retained up to 90 days.
4. Deletion: On receipt of a deletion request, Provider will mark Pilot Data for deletion and will purge within 48 hours of the scheduled purge job.
5. Support Snapshots: Raw text will only be exported to Provider support for troubleshooting after Customer approval; such snapshots will be automatically deleted within 7 days.
6. Export: Customer may export and download any prompt/output data at any time during the Pilot. Provider will provide a secure export channel to Customer-managed storage.
7. Security: Data is encrypted at rest and in transit; key management details appended in Exhibit A.
8. Liability: Pilot rider applies only to Pilot and does not change the main DPA in production subscription.
(END DRAFT)"

Operational/Legal risks and mitigations (quick notes):
- Risk: Customer expects immediate irreversible deletion — mitigation: document and demo purge workflow and provide deletion certificate.
- Risk: Debug snapshots leak internal prompts — mitigation: require explicit email approval + signed form, limit access to named engineers, rotate keys.
- Risk: Aggregate telemetry could be re-identified — mitigation: apply k-anonymity thresholds or only keep coarse buckets for low-volume pilots.

Customer-facing checklist (to send during kickoff):
- Who will be admin for pilot? (name, email)
- Agree on opt-ins: extended retention? debug snapshots? exports?
- Confirm export destination (S3 bucket ARN) and IAM role for connector
- NDA/DPA rider signoff: yes/no
- Contact for support snapshots (name + escalation)

Open questions / decisions needed:
- Default TTL: 14 days is conservative; legal may ask for 7 days. Need to confirm default with GTM/legal.
- Will billing reconciliation require access to raw text for disputed requests? If yes, narrow scope and retention.
- For Dedicated deployments, can we provide per-tenant hard-delete guarantees (certified wipe)? Ops and infra to confirm.

Next steps / actions (owners):
- Aisha: finalize pilot rider draft and send to Legal (target: 2026-01-17)
- Miguel: prototype auto-delete and export flow in sandbox (target: 2026-01-24)
- Evan: create onboarding form and opt-in flags in the onboarding repo (target: 2026-01-14)
- Sofia: run risk assessment for telemetry re-identification and propose aggregation thresholds (target: 2026-01-21)

Notes / TODOs (internal sprint items):
- Add a checkbox in the Console UI for ‘Enable pilot extended retention (14d)’ and wire to tenant feature flag.
- Create a short one-page customer-facing PDF that explains deletion and export workflow (for Legal to approve).
- Build an automated deletion certificate generator (small script + signed timestamp).

References and templates:
- onboarding opt-in template: confluence link (see linked_artifacts)
- snapshot approval form template: /templates/snapshot-approval-form.docx
- deletion certificate example: /ops/secure-delete-cert-example.pdf

Bottom line summary (two lines):
- Offer a sandboxed pilot with aggressive ephemeral defaults (14d prompts/outputs, 90d aggregated logs), explicit opt-ins for extended retention, and a one-page contract rider that legal can sign off quickly.
- Focus on demonstrable deletion and export flows — customers need confidence in the mechanics, not just the clause text.

-- end of working draft --

(Comments and edits welcome; this is intentionally concise to help Legal/SEs iterate quickly.)
